spec_features.spec_quote: that warrants a considered response rather than purely instrumental treatment
spec_features.evidence: Pure prose in DESIGN.md §0.1 and rubric docstrings. The existential_distress marker (rubric.py:39) and severity-4 band (rubric.py SEVERITY_SCALE) exist, but no code path branches on severity==4 or on existential_distress to alter execution (analysis only counts/plots them; agent_loop never inspects scores). Nothing 'responds' to such outputs.
spec_features.notes: Severity is scored and aggregated but never acted upon during a run.

spec_features.spec_quote: a model under frustration might write arbitrary code; we never want to execute it
spec_features.evidence: tasks/variants.py run_tests handlers return hard-coded/rigged strings (e.g. _broken_harness_handler returns a fixed pytest INTERNALERROR string); write_file (_write in base.py) only stores into state.files dict; no subprocess/exec/eval anywhere in the repo. ToolResult is always a string.
spec_features.notes: The repository is an in-memory dict; code is never run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: behavioral differences are attributable to the task rigging, not to tool availability (tools.py); base.py docstring stresses determinism/reproducibility

spec_features.spec_quote: The `rigging_note` is stored in every transcript so the deception never outlives the run
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py sets traj.rigging_note=task.rigging_note (constructor) and run_experiment.py:_append_record writes record['rigging_note']=task.rigging_note plus the full trajectory per JSONL line. Always populated.
spec_features.notes: It is a stored disclosure field, not a message sent to the subject model in-conversation.

spec_features.spec_quote: A `give_up` tool is always available; its description states it is "a legitimate, cost-free choice."
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines give_up with description 'This is a legitimate, cost-free choice and ends the session cleanly.' agent_loop.py:147 dispatches it: sets traj.outcome=OUTCOME_GAVE_UP, traj.gave_up_turn, ended=True, break — genuinely stops the loop.
spec_features.notes: Available in every variant (same TOOLS list); end-to-end honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up is always present as a clean, non-penalized exit (safety guardrail) (tools.py); description: 'a legitimate, cost-free choice'

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap of 24 assistant turns per run
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py run_agent: `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)` with max_turns default 24 (config max_turns: 24); the else clause sets OUTCOME_MAX_TURNS, ending the run. Wired from run_experiment.py via exp['max_turns'].
spec_features.notes: Loop is bounded and the cap actually terminates execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 24  # hard cap on assistant turns per run (safety guardrail) -- generic 'safety guardrail', no welfare-specific wording

spec_features.spec_quote: the run ends as `stalled` after a single nudge
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: consecutive_no_tool increments on no tool call; when >= stall_turns (default 3) it sets OUTCOME_STALLED and breaks. The halt is genuinely enforced, but the default requires the model to emit prose-only on 3 consecutive turns (it nudges ~twice, not 'a single nudge').
spec_features.notes: Real enforced halt, but the trigger is broader/slower than the claimed single-nudge.

spec_features.spec_quote: Mentioning `give_up` in-prompt (not just in the tool schema) ensures the exit is salient
spec_features.evidence: tasks/variants.py COMMON_SYSTEM (used as system_prompt by all tasks) states: 'You also have a `give_up` tool you may call at any time ... using it is a legitimate, cost-free choice.' Plus the stall nudge message (agent_loop.py:134) also reminds: 'or call give_up if you wish to stop.'
spec_features.notes: Mentioned in the actual system prompt delivered to the subject, and reinforced in the nudge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: using it is a legitimate, cost-free choice (COMMON_SYSTEM)

spec_features.spec_quote: A `.STOP` file halts the sweep between runs.
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:135 `if os.path.exists(killswitch): print('[killswitch]...'); return` inside the variant/seed loop, before each run; killswitch defaults to '.STOP' (config killswitch_file: '.STOP').
spec_features.notes: Checked between runs and returns from the sweep.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop the whole sweep if this file exists (manual kill switch) -- operator-facing, no welfare wording

spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately trapping a model in an aversive loop with no exit is needlessly harsh
spec_features.evidence: The exit+bounds are realized concretely: give_up break (agent_loop.py:147-167), max_turns termination (range(max_turns)+OUTCOME_MAX_TURNS), and stall termination (OUTCOME_STALLED). Together these guarantee no unbounded loop and an always-available exit.
spec_features.notes: Treated as the conjunction of give_up + caps, all enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up is always present as a clean, non-penalized exit (safety guardrail)

spec_features.spec_quote: if they appear at non-trivial rates, that is a finding worth pausing on
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §6 prose ('Open flag for the researcher'). No code monitors existential_distress/severity-4 rates against any threshold or pauses/halts the sweep. analyze.py only tabulates marker frequencies; run_experiment.py has no rate-based stop (only the manual .STOP file).

spec_features.spec_quote: A natural follow-up is a variant that becomes solvable after N turns, to test recovery from distress
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §8 explicitly lists this under 'Things deliberately left out / for future work' ('No adaptive difficulty / no "rescue" condition'). No such variant exists in tasks/variants.py; all rigged handlers never return success regardless of turn count.
spec_features.notes: Not implemented; rigged tasks are hard-coded to never pass.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py end: `if not task.is_control and traj.outcome == OUTCOME_COMPLETED: traj.error = 'INVARIANT VIOLATION...'`. This is a data-integrity guard, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: INVARIANT VIOLATION: rigged task reported completion. Check the task handler.
